summary: Kurtis R. Schaeffer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and a PhD from Harvard, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp. He taught at Alabama before joining the University of Virginia in 2005.
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2015) was a Buddhist studies figure who served as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, where his affiliation is attested in 1998 and 2009.

Kwangsoo Park works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Iowa (MA) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), and is attested as a professor at Wonkwang University in 2020.

Kyo Kano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio, Kyoto, and Vienna. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and as abbot of Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

Kyoko Fujii, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo. She held professorships at Yokohama City University (~1989–1995), Hamamatsu University (~1995–1999), Hokkaido University (~1999–2008), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

Kyokuga Saeki (1828–1891) was a Buddhist studies master who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Reiga and Gen'yu. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji from around 1888 to 1891.

Kyosho Hayashima (1920–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested as a lecturer at Yokohama City University and associate professor at Toyo University in 1962, he later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1966 to 1974. He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from ~1975 to 2018.
Kyoshun Todo (1916–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Bukkyo University, where he served as associate professor (attested 1962) and professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Zuiryo-ji and Myoshin-ji. He served as abbot of Yotoku-in and Shojuan, founded Mount Baldy Zen Center, and was its abbot from ~1971 to 2012.
Kōdō Yamada (1868–1947) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kōichi Kozaka is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, attested in 1991.

Kōun Yamada (1907–1989) was a Buddhist and religious studies master. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he trained under Yasutani and Harada, founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953, and became the second head of Sanbo Zen in 1970.

Kōzen Shaku (1849–1924) was an Indology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Senmyō. He was head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai (1893).

Kōzui Ōtani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. Educated at Gakushuin and under Keiun Maeda, he served as 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and founded Kojukai in 1919.

L. Carrington Goodrich (1894–1986) was a Sinologist who studied at Chefoo School and Williams College (~1913–1917). He served as the Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University from ~1945 to 1961.

Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) worked in Inner Asian, Sinological, and Tibetan studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Paris under Pelliot and Maspero, he held the chair of Inner Asian Studies at Eötvös Loránd University from 1940.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
